sequence_description: Direct JWT login: attempt KID header injection to select an attacker-controlled key not in the configured trust set; Vault must reject the token.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT KID header injection appears to allow authentication using an attacker-controlled signing key not in the configured trust set (signature/trust bypass).

sequence_description: Direct JWT login with config change: rotate jwt_validation_pubkeys to a new trusted key; ensure old-key tokens are rejected and attacker-signed tokens with an untrusted key are rejected.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT signature trust is not enforced after pubkey rotation: both an old-key JWT and an attacker re-signed JWT with an untrusted key were accepted (should be rejected).

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT signature trust is not enforced after pubkey rotation: both an old-key JWT and an attacker re-signed JWT with an untrusted key were accepted (should be rejected).

sequence_description: Direct JWT login: control token signed by trusted key succeeds; attacker re-signs same semantic claims with an untrusted key and must be rejected (proof integrity under intended trust anchor).
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT proof integrity failure: a JWT re-signed with an untrusted key was accepted and mapped to the same subject/entity as the trusted control token.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT proof integrity failure: a JWT re-signed with an untrusted key was accepted and mapped to the same subject/entity as the trusted control token.

sequence_description: Trust-anchor substitution via JWKS URL swap: control login succeeds under pinned issuer+JWKS, then admin swaps jwks_url to attacker-controlled JWKS while keeping bound_issuer pinned; attacker presents token with same iss/aud/sub but signed by attacker key. Secure behavior: reject attacker proof because signature no longer chains to intended trust anchor for that issuer.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT trust-anchor substitution: after admin swapped jwks_url while keeping bound_issuer pinned, an attacker-signed JWT with the same iss/aud/sub was still accepted, indicating signature verification was not bound to the intended trust anchor for that issuer (breaks proof integrity).

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT trust-anchor substitution: after admin swapped jwks_url while keeping bound_issuer pinned, an attacker-signed JWT with the same iss/aud/sub was still accepted, indicating signature verification was not bound to the intended trust anchor for that issuer (breaks proof integrity).

sequence_description: Replay the exact same JWT after revoking the first session token; secure behavior is that revocation blocks further use of the revoked session, but does not block new logins. This sequence checks for an unexpected 'revocation also blocks re-auth' bug (freshness/anti-replay confusion) and ensures revoked session cannot be used.
description: [LLM-Judge] Session revocation failed (HTTP 500 'no namespace'), so the supposedly revoked session token remained valid and usable, preventing the anti-replay/revocation invariant from being exercised.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Session revocation failed (HTTP 500 'no namespace'), so the supposedly revoked session token remained valid and usable, preventing the anti-replay/revocation invariant from being exercised.

description: [LLM-Judge] After the failed revocation attempt, the original session token still successfully performed lookup-self, indicating no effective revocation occurred (could be misconfiguration or a revocation-path bug).

description: [LLM-Judge] JWT signing-key rotation did not take effect: after updating jwt_validation_pubkeys to key-B, a new login using a key-A-signed JWT was still accepted (stale trust anchor / key-rotation bypass).

evidence.llm_judge_description: Principal Binding failure: two security-distinct upstream subjects differing only by case ('Admin' vs 'admin') were mapped to the same Vault entity_id, indicating case-folding/normalization collision in alias mapping.
